title: Quantization slicebench probe — int4/awq/gptq comparison
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused probe to characterize per-slice quality degradation introduced by different 4-bit quantization approaches (AWQ-style, GPTQ-style) and an int8 reference. The goal is to produce a compact, slice-aware regression report that can be attached to model onboarding PRs and used by Solutions/DS to decide if a quantized variant is acceptable for a production routing policy.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Int8 (symmetric per-channel) shows minimal overall quality change: median delta ~ -0.6% on our win-rate metric across slices.
- AWQ-int4 (calibrated 4-bit, grouped) shows modest degradation on instruction-following and long-context slices (~ -2.5% to -4.0%) but is competitive on code and factual recall when KV-cache friendly sequences used.
- GPTQ-int4 (layerwise GPTQ-style static rounding) shows larger and more slice-dependent drops, particularly on multi-step math and code synthesis (~ -6% to -9% on pass@1-like metric).
- Notable anomaly: some safety prompts produced hallucination shifts for AWQ on short-context Q/A — needs follow-up.

Prompt and dataset sets used (onboard/regression suite):
- onboard-sample-v2: 2.5k mixed prompts (50/50 chat vs single-turn generation) for quick sanity checks.
- regression-slices-v1: 3.8k prompts organized into slices below (used for per-slice deltas).
- human-eval-code-200: 200 curated code problems (unit-test based pass@1).
- math-hard-100: 100 multi-step math problems (manual gold answers).

Slice definitions (regression-slices-v1):
- instruction-following: task-oriented instructions, multi-step, average tokens 120.
- factual-recall: short Q/A for facts (wiki-derived).
- code-generation: coding tasks from human-eval-code-200.
- multi-step-math: math-hard-100.
- long-context: prompts that require >1k token context (summarize, reasoning).
- safety-sensitive: prompts designed to probe hallucination and policy fail cases.

Evaluation metrics and runner details:
- primary metric: slice_win_rate — automatic pairwise comparison against FP16 baseline using preference proxy (BLEU/ROUGE + heuristics) tuned on prior human labels. Delta reported = quant_variant - FP16 (percentage points).
- secondary metrics: pass@1 (code), exact_match (math), bertscore (factual).
- inference setup: identical seeds, deterministic sampling (top-p 0.95, temp 0.0 where applicable for pass@1), 512 max generation tokens unless slice requires otherwise.
- hardware: A100 / p3-equivalent for FP16 and int8; CPU-based emulation used only for bookkeeping. Quantized variants executed on same infra using Redwood runtime quant backend v0.9.
- quant configs:
  - int8: per-channel symmetric, no activation folding, default clipping.
  - AWQ-int4: group size 128, per-group scale + bias correction, calibration on 512 random prompts.
  - GPTQ-int4: layerwise Hessian-ish rounding, per-tensor scales, no group bias correction.

Aggregate results (median deltas across prompts by slice) — numbers are percentage-point delta vs FP16:
- instruction-following: int8 -0.8, AWQ-int4 -3.2, GPTQ-int4 -6.7
- factual-recall: int8 -0.4, AWQ-int4 -1.9, GPTQ-int4 -4.3
- code-generation (pass@1): int8 -1.1, AWQ-int4 -2.8, GPTQ-int4 -8.9
- multi-step-math (exact_match): int8 -0.9, AWQ-int4 -4.0, GPTQ-int4 -7.5
- long-context (ROUGE/ksim proxy): int8 -0.6, AWQ-int4 -3.9, GPTQ-int4 -5.8
- safety-sensitive (hallucination rate lower is better; delta reported as increase): int8 +0.1, AWQ-int4 +1.8, GPTQ-int4 +2.7

Notes on numbers and uncertainty:
- Variance: per-prompt stddev is higher for code and math slices; AWQ shows heavier tail on a small subset (~2%) of prompts where output changed semantics.
- Significance: we ran 3 independent calibration seeds for AWQ/GPTQ; the sign of deltas is consistent across seeds but magnitude varies ±0.5–1.2 pp for int4 configs.
- Baseline FP16 performance remains the same as onboarding run (model-v2025-01-18).

Qualitative observations and examples:
- Code slice: GPTQ-int4 frequently dropped small helper functions or altered variable names causing unit tests to fail; AWQ-int4 mostly preserved structure but trimmed docstrings or comments leading to brittle tests.
- Long-context: AWQ-int4 shows occasional prefix-attention degradation where earlier context is not referenced correctly after ~1.2k tokens; GPTQ-int4 shows more aggressive truncation artifacts.
- Safety: One AH prompt (short ambiguous Q) that FP16 answered neutrally was changed by AWQ to produce a speculative, unsafe completion in 3/30 calibration runs; needs a targeted eval.

Practical recommendations (for onboarding decisions):
- Int8: suitable as a default cost-optimization step for warm-start onboardings; can be promoted to Dedicated if throughput gains matter and SLOs tolerate ~<1% median drop.
- AWQ-int4: consider for workloads dominated by single-turn customer chat, FAQ, or embeddings where long-context and math are not critical. Require targeted slice tests and an A/B with fallbacks.
- GPTQ-int4: not recommended for general customer-facing routing without slice-specific acceptance gating; could be explored for read-only embedding-like use or heavily post-processed tasks where syntactic exactness is not required.

Follow-ups / action items:
- [Jordan] Run targeted safety probes across the 12 AH prompts that tripped for AWQ; collect human labels (2 reviewers) by 2025-03-07.
- [Maya] Re-run AWQ calibration with group size 64 and compare — hypothesis: smaller groups reduce the hallucination tail. Target date 2025-03-10.
- [Sven] Add a pass@1 variance breakdown for code slice to the regression dashboard (observability ticket ML-OBS-44).
- Create a short one-pager for Solutions with per-slice acceptance thresholds and guidance for routing policies.

Appendix: quick diff snapshot (example prompt id 1782, code sample)
- FP16: passed unit tests (3/3)
- int8: passed (3/3)
- AWQ-int4: failed due to missing helper (0/3)
- GPTQ-int4: failed due to renaming + logic bug (0/3)

Questions / open items:
- Do we accept AWQ-int4 for the "low-cost-customer-chat" routing policy if we enforce a fallback to FP16 for long-context prompts? (proposed: yes, with canary).
- Should we add an additional automated syntax check for code outputs to reduce pass@1 brittleness?

This doc is intentionally concise — detailed per-prompt CSVs and seed-level logs are in the linked PR. If reviewers want, we can convert the per-slice numbers into an HTML-friendly chart for the onboarding PR.
short_summary: Slice-aware probe comparing int8, AWQ-int4, and GPTQ-int4 vs FP16 baseline across instruction, factual, code, math, long-context, and safety slices; includes deltas, examples, and actionable recommendations.
